scope.flow: ServiceManager.registerAgents agent-instance registration for a service

entities.name: service with many slots in ActiveRegistration state

statements.text: An attacker can create a service with many slots for the purpose of the attack.
The service can be created without the intention to push it to deploy, kept at ActiveRegistration state to register instances.
The victim's address is an operator address used to register agent instances.
A malicious operator registers agent instances for a service using another operator's address as an instance address.

Neither ServiceManager.registerAgents nor ServiceRegistry.registerAgents checks whether the given instance addresses are already in use as operator addresses, so the victim's operator address is accepted as an instance address and the victim is permanently blocked from registering any agent instance for any service in the future.
The attack cannot be stopped by pausing the ServiceManager because there is no pause check in ServiceManager.registerAgents.

An operator address must not be usable as an agent instance address while it is in use as an operator address; it may only be used as an instance address after its registered instance count reaches zero.
An operator must be able to register instances for many services with the same address.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker must be a registered/whitelisted operator for the target service or how the attacker obtains authorization to register instances.
Report does not specify the exact state transition or prior transaction establishing the victim's operator registration beyond the general claim that operators use addresses to register instances.
The permanent-block outcome is described as a consequence of the missing collision check; the precise revert/error on the victim's later registration is not given.
Whether the attacker's service must be in ActiveRegistration at the moment of registration is implied but not stated as a strict precondition.
